Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

humour noun

also humor, sense of humour, sense of humor, wit, humorous, witty, humorously

classical

Cic. Brut. 177: fēstīvitāte et facētiīs C. Jūlius omnibus praestitit (Lewis & Short, s.v. fēstīvitās)
Cic. Or. 87 (Lewis & Short)

facētiae, facētiārum f. pl.

noun, first declension, plural · Declension on Wiktionary

wit, humour, witty sayings

Humour in speech and behaviour, and the jokes themselves. The adjective is facētus, witty.

Other words

  • lepōs (lepor), lepōris m. — charm, wit, pleasantry

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.134: sī jocōsīs, lepōrem · Declension on Wiktionary

    First charm and grace of manner; of speech, light, pleasant humour, Cicero’s most frequent use (Lewis & Short).

  • fēstīvitās, fēstīvitātis f. — good humour, jollity; humour in speech

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 2.219 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 154; Traupman 330 · Declension on Wiktionary

    Cheerful high spirits, and of speech, humour; in Plautus a pet name (mea fēstīvitās). Traupman’s word for humour, with fēstīvus for humorous.

  • sal, salis m. — wit (literally salt)

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 9.15.2: Rōmānī veterēs atque urbānī salēs (Lewis & Short); Hor. Ep. 2.2.60: sale nigrō, biting wit (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    Sharp, salty wit, often biting; salēs, witticisms.

  • fēstīvē — humorously, wittily

    also used · classical · Traupman 154

Examples

  • est enim lepōrum differtus puer ac facētiārum

    for the boy is stuffed full of charm and witCatull. 12.8–9

  • sī sēriīs, sevēritātem adhibeat, sī jocōsīs, lepōrem

    for serious things let him bring gravity, for playful ones a light touchCic. Off. 1.134

See also funny, joke.
